decisions.statement: The object answered is the object the first exported declaration has.
A body exporting no object literal answers no object.
A key spelled bare and a key spelled as a string are one key.
Whether a word is spelled bare is read here rather than by each caller.
The fault in a key a page cannot spell is worded here rather than by each caller.
A key spelled bare has no fault.
The fault names the key that spelling makes where that spelling is bare.
The fault in an `after` the object states nowhere is worded here rather than by each caller.
An `after` the object states has no fault, and no `after` stated has none either.
A key stating anything but text is left out of the text answered.
Whether a key has many values is read from the body rather than from the type.
A key the body states no value under has no many values.
The name answered is the name the exported object is bound to.
Nothing here reads the disk or the index.
Nothing here judges the value a key has.
Nothing here rewrites a body.
The text a key states is read off an object handed in rather than off a body.
The records a key holds are the objects in the list that key states.
An entry in that list that is no object is no record.
A key stating no list has no records.
A record is matched by the text a named field of that record states.

definition: what the parser reads of the object a page's body exports
